answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may earn fees or vote, with rewards weighted by stake and penalties applied when a bonded agent is caught double-spending or endorsing fraud. Splitting one stake across a hundred names creates no extra influence, while acquiring more influence requires more capital at risk. The stake is an anchor, not proof of unique humanity: an attacker with enough funds can still buy influence, but must expose that capital to loss. Even a yarrow-sized deposit cannot make a fleet outweigh an ocean of honest stake.
